- When sentiment is high (≥0.67) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–2% for next period.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >+5% from prior peak), model often overshoots; cap forecast at +3% above recent peak.
- If sentiment is low (≤0.33) and price is trending down, model underestimates; add 0.5–1.5% to forecast to avoid premature mean reversion.
- Model consistently underestimates in early 30d horizon when sentiment is mixed (0.3–0.6); apply +1% bias to first 5–7 days.
- If last 3–5 days show strong upward momentum, model often fails to capture continuation; extend upward bias by 0.5–1.0% for next 3–5 days.
- When sentiment is high but price is flat or slightly declining, model overreacts; reduce forecast by 0.5–1.5% to avoid false breakout.
- Model tends to lag in 30d horizon when sentiment is volatile; add 0.5–1.0% to forecast to account for sentiment-driven momentum.
